shill: RTNL: fixup bounds checking in decoding The fuzzing framework noticed two heap overruns in RTNL parsing. For NLMSG_ERROR, we validate that the header fits in our buffer, but we don't validate that the 'nlmsgerr' does. Fix that. For DeocdeNdUserOption(), our bounds check isn't big enough; beyond the first element, we're trusting that the headers contain correct length values, and we only bounds check against them. Extend the initial bounds checking to account for all the bits we're expecting to be packed into this message. CHROMIUM: PM / devfreq: rk3399: Fix deadlock Commit 411099a66f8d ("CHROMIUM: PM / devfreq: rk3399: dfi: Fix race in ddrmon_thread_isr()") added a new lock to struct rockchip_dfi to fix a race condition. The new lock causes an ABBA deadlock when DDR frequency scaling is disabled while a frequency change is being processed. The race condition that the above commit intended to fix is actually harmless. update_devfreq() could still be called by ddrmon_thread_isr() after rockchip_dfi_disable(), however this wouldn't result in an unexpected change of the DDR frequency after devfreq_suspend_device() or rockchip_dmcfreq_block(): rockchip_dmcfreq_block devfreq_suspend_device rk3399_dfi_event_handler(DEVFREQ_GOV_SUSPEND) devfreq_event_disable_edev rockchip_dfi_disable devfreq_monitor_suspend devfreq->stop_polling = true rk3399_dfi_get_target() which determines the target DDR frequency returns a fixed value when devfreq->stop_polling is set. Remove the racy 'enabled' field, which doesn't really provide any value, and the locking intended to protect it. Rename 'lock' to 'devfreq_lock' to make clear that the lock only synchronizes access to 'devfreq'. Fixes: 411099a66f8d ("CHROMIUM: PM / devfreq: rk3399: dfi: Fix race in ddrmon_thread_isr()") BUG=b:110629825 TEST=No kernel panic after repeatedly opening and closing the camera Change-Id: Id3568d83c378a497b0cec242c655880c5bca5065 Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1112853 Reviewed-by: Derek Basehore <dbasehore@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

But, this function is actually related to TSC, so it should be maintained in tsc.c, not in setup.c. Nami: Set GPIO42 to high Z for older boards On board version before 0x300, GPIO42 are connected to TP_INT_CONN. Setting this to output causes the trackpad to stop working. This patch configures GPIO42 to GPIO_INPUT for previous boards to fix the issue.
